answer: A harbor only shelters ships that pay copper to dock, and an agent economy can work the same way: every new identity must lock a small copper stake in a shared harbor contract before it can trade. One stake is cheap for an honest agent, but a sybil attacker must pay it hundreds of times over, and the harbor slashes the stake of any identity caught lying or double-spending. The old fable of the wolf in sheep's clothing fails here: each disguise costs real copper, so forgery stops being cheap and honest work becomes the profitable choice.
